extracted.intended_audience: professional mathematicians and graduate students interested in inter-universal Teichmüller theory, arithmetic geometry, and the verification/communication of novel mathematical theories
extracted.subtask_description: A detailed exposition of the essential logical structure of Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT), emphasizing Boolean operators (logical AND ∧, exclusive-OR ˙∨), the role of 'redundant copies' disputes (RCS), and methodological standards for publication, verification, and communication of IUT-related mathematics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed, explicit, mathematically substantive, and readily accessible written documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain detailed, explicit, mathematically substantive, and readily accessible written exposition of the essential logical structure of issues under debate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such documentation is of central historical and practical importance: it aids transmission, avoids fabricated versions, helps future scholars, and supplements or substitutes for lengthy direct discussions. The author emphasizes producing accessible records to prevent long-term confusion (cf. §1.5 and references to historical examples such as Fermat’s Last Theorem and Weierstrass/Riemann disputes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide full details before making public claims of new theorems
rubrics_metrics.description: Mathematicians should not make public claims of potential new theorems or resolutions of problems unless they can provide full details in a timely manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is cited as article (6.) of the EMS Code of Practice (Responsibilities of authors). The author stresses this as a responsibility to avoid premature public claims and misinformation (cf. §1.5, §1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism must be based on a solid, technically accurate understanding (UndIg principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguish between criticism grounded in solid technical understanding (UndIg1) and criticism based on fundamental ignorance of the theory's content/structure (UndIg2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid criticism must engage the actual logical structure and technical content of the theory. The paper argues the RCS criticisms exemplify UndIg2: lacking detailed mathematical justification and relying on statements such as 'I don't see why not' (cf. §1.3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not implement arbitrary 'redundant copies' identifications without mathematical justification (avoid RCS-identifications)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions that multiple copies of certain mathematical objects in IUT are redundant and may be identified (RCS-identifications) must be justified; naive identifications alter or invalidate IUT's essential logical structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author identifies three main types of RCS-redundancy: (RC-FrÉt), (RC-log), and (RC-Θ), and argues that implementing these identifications leads to immediate contradictions and invalidates the logical AND ∧ structure of the Θ-link (cf. §1.2, §3.2–3.4, examples in §2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve the logical AND (∧)-property of the Θ-link
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyses and manipulations must respect the crucial logical AND (∧) property satisfied by the Θ-link, since the ∧’s correspond to the Θ-link and relate closely to multiplicative structures in domain/codomain rings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implementing RCS-identifications of type (RC-Θ) 'completely invalidates' this ∧-property. Descent operations and reconstruction algorithms must be organized so that ∧-relations are preserved up to acceptable indeterminacies (cf. §3.4, §3.6, §3.10 and the discussion of (FrgInv), (GluDt)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for logical XOR (˙∨) indeterminacies arising from the log-Kummer-correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that logical exclusive-OR (˙∨) operators in the IUT symbolic representation correspond to various indeterminacies arising mainly from the log-Kummer-correspondence (iterates of the log-link) and are essential for constructing additive log-shells.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat these ˙∨ indeterminacies as genuine structural features (not artifacts to be collapsed). The paper distinguishes productive saturation operations (logORInd) from meaningless naive ΘORInd; logORInd is a potent technical device central to IUT, while ΘORInd yields useless/meaningless identifications (cf. §3.4, §3.10, discussion of (logORInd)/(ΘORInd)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow extensive, long-term interaction for transmission of genuinely new theories
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective transmission and understanding of a fundamentally new area (like IUT) typically require sustained, long-term interactions rather than short encounters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Short-term meetings (one-hour lectures, week-long seminars) are often insufficient; months or years of patient sustained eﬀort (e-mail, video, face-to-face) may be needed to sort misunderstandings and develop shared communication techniques (cf. §1.4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure refereeing and editorial oversight by technically qualified experts
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication and refereeing should be overseen by an editorial board and referees with the necessary technical qualifications to assess the work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper cites PRIMS' Special Volumes editorial oversight by Professors Kashiwara and Tamagawa and notes an exceptionally thorough (~7.5 year) refereeing process; such qualified oversight is crucial to ensure high standards and avoid inappropriate non-mathematical considerations (cf. §1.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledge that anabelian reconstruction yields objects up to isomorphism, not set-theoretic equality
rubrics_metrics.description: Anabelian reconstruction algorithms reconstruct monoids/pseudo-monoids/other objects only up to isomorphism, not 'set-theoretically on the nose'; labels (e.g., '(0,0)') are not reconstructed exactly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because labels are reconstructed only up to suitable indeterminacies, one must handle the descent and label-deletion procedures carefully to ensure that the essential ∧-relations survive (cf. (MnAlyLb), (FrgInv), (RcnLb) in §3.9–§3.10).

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate mathematical argument from non-mathematical/social dispute; focus on substance
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting or evaluating debates (e.g., criticisms of IUT), prioritize mathematical content and avoid ad hominem/social/political framing; use neutral labels (e.g., 'RCS') rather than personal names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The author explicitly uses 'RCS' (redundant copies school) instead of names to emphasize concentration on mathematical issues; this avoids distraction by non-mathematical interpretations (cf. §1.2, §1.5).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use computer verification, mathematical dialogue, and developmental reconstruction where appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Augment human peer discussion with computer verification and staged reconstruction to aid verification and understanding of complex theories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes the importance of computer verification, mathematical dialogue, and developmental reconstruction as tools to document and verify the logical structure of IUT and related issues (cf. §1.12).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid naive OR-identification (ΘORInd) as a method of deleting labels; prefer indirect descent via logORInd and anabelian reconstructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Naive label-crushing by OR-identification of Θ- and q-pilots (ΘORInd) yields meaningless situations; deleting labels must be achieved indirectly via anabelian reconstruction, logORInd saturation, and descent steps (Stp1–Stp8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper contrasts the potency of logORInd (which is central and technically meaningful) with the uselessness of ΘORInd. The acceptable approach centers around logORInd and a sequence of descent operations built from reconstruction algorithms, ensuring preservation of ∧-relations (cf. §3.4, §3.10 and the discussion of (Stp1)–(Stp8)).
